title: A scripted codex double drives the real MCP wire to verifier ACCEPTED and lander COMMITTED
description:
SPIDR grandchild B of task-df64aa204d6f4c35810376226980e4b7 (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05). dependsOn grandchild A task-48932becda314704aad652b49a8d2209, which lands the codex tool-roster and result-size parity this journey exercises. This row is the OFFLINE PROOF.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: a codex-shaped scripted double plus one e2e journey that drives it over the REAL MCP wire to a durable ACCEPTED and COMMITTED.

THE MODEL TO COPY EXISTS. Measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): tests/e2e/foundation/fake-agent.mjs (315 lines) is already a real-wire double - it opens an MCP session over HTTP with the scoped bearer, calls work_get_context, review_submit and work_release as real JSON-RPC tools/call frames, and never touches the store directly. tests/e2e/foundation/j1-loop-harness.ts:320 writeAgentShim writes the shim and hands it to the wrapper as MOE_AGENT_COMMAND (:360); tests/e2e/foundation/j1-ledger-view.ts reads every verdict off the durable ledger after the processes are dead. Copy that shape.

THREE MEASURED CONSTRAINTS THE PLAN MUST RESPECT.

(1) THE SHIM MUST BE NAMED EXACTLY `codex.cmd` / `codex.sh`. The codex path is selected by the basename regex at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts:~80, `/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu`. The existing writeAgentShim emits `agent-<arm>.cmd`, and `agent-codex.cmd` does NOT match that regex - the character before "codex" is a hyphen, not a path separator or the start of the string. A shim named the existing way silently runs the CLAUDE branch and the journey proves nothing about codex.

(2) THE DOUBLE READS ITS CREDENTIAL DIFFERENTLY FROM fake-agent.mjs. A claude seat gets a JSON file at `--mcp-config`; a codex seat gets NEITHER. The bearer arrives in the child's own environment under MOE_AGENT_MCP_BEARER (agent-spawner.ts:37 CODEX_BEARER_VARIABLE, injected at :156 after the agentEnvironment spread, pinned by agent-spawner.test.ts:291) and the origin arrives as the argv pair `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.url=<origin>`. So the codex double parses its origin off argv and reads its bearer from env - the exact inverse of fake-agent.mjs, which deliberately treats argv flags as non-evidence.

(3) `planning.submit_decomposition` IS WITHHELD FROM THE V2 REGISTRY. apps/daemon/src/daemon-v2-command-registry.ts:211 puts it in a `withheld` set "until its `/2` service consumes the authority-safe compiler", deliberately preferring a visible roster failure to a v1 fallback. The journey therefore must dispatch it through a daemon that is NOT running the v2 marker, or assert the exact roster refusal instead. Determine which before writing the arm.

THIS ROW DOES NOT NEED THE DURABLE PROVIDER SETTING. Because the codex branch is selected by the shim's NAME, the offline proof does not depend on task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605 or its grandchildren. Do not add that dependency.

NOT IN SCOPE: the real `codex exec` run and the Seats provider disclosure (child 3, task-c090faae9fbe438b959e76a08b7dcfdb, explicitly allowed to block on quota); the spawn-surface parity itself (grandchild A); no UI.

VERIFY: `pnpm test:e2e`.
definitionOfDone: A scripted codex double drives the REAL MCP wire end to end offline against a real daemon: the planning reads, then `planning.submit_decomposition` accepted, then a `node.deliver` reaching verifier ACCEPTED and lander COMMITTED. The double opens its own MCP session with the scoped bearer and calls real tools/call frames - it NEVER writes to the store directly, or the journey proves the fixture instead of the product.

Every verdict is asserted from the DURABLE STORE after the processes are dead - the sealed run, the verifier receipt, and the landing sha - never from the double's own exit code or its stdout. A double that exits 0 without landing must fail this journey; add that negative arm the way fake-agent.mjs's `skip-review` arm does.

The work_get_context / work_release path completes for a codex seat: the double claims, reads its own item, and RELEASES ON THE FIRST TRY, reusing the observed-version disclosure that task-f99cec0b landed at apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-conflict-error.ts (`conflictError(decision)`, :53). Assert the release decision is EFFECTS_COMMITTED - not merely that the call returned, and not merely that it did not throw.

The shim the journey writes is named so the spawner's codex regex actually selects the codex branch, and an arm PROVES the codex branch ran (assert on the codex-shaped argv or the bearer-in-env path, not on the shim's filename) - otherwise a rename silently reverts this journey to testing the claude seat.

`pnpm test:e2e` count line quoted with the new test named in the output. Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`.
taskRails: OFFLINE PROOF ONLY. The real `codex exec` run is child 3's live drive; the Codex quota was exhausted until 2026-09-08 and this row must not depend on it.
THE DOUBLE GOES THROUGH THE REAL MCP WIRE with the scoped bearer and NEVER writes to the store directly - otherwise the journey proves the fixture, not the product.

NEVER WEAKEN THE CODEX SPAWN SURFACE to make the journey pass: `--ignore-user-config`, the bearer through the env var name, the closed env allowlist and the quote-free `-c` values are deliberate. If one blocks the journey, report it rather than relaxing it.

The double must be plain `.mjs` runnable under bare `node` - node builtins only, no TypeScript, no dependency, deliberately outside the e2e tsconfig - for the same reason fake-agent.mjs is (see its header comment). Do not add it to tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json.

DO NOT EDIT fake-agent.mjs to serve both providers. It documents at length that it treats argv flags as non-evidence and learns everything from the spawner; the codex double inverts exactly that (bearer from env, origin from argv). Fold the two together and both stop proving what they were written to prove.

`pnpm test:e2e` runs `tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json` FIRST, so a type error in the harness fails the leg before a single test runs. Read the output for the `Test Files N passed` count line; a tsc failure is not a test result.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE, DECIDE THE TWO OPEN QUESTIONS, NO EDITS. (a) CONFIRM THE PREREQUISITE LANDED. task-48932bec (grandchild A) owns the codex tool-roster and result-size parity this journey exercises. Prove it at the tree rather than from the board, and read its completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings for the exact codex argv it left behind - this row asserts against that argv, so a stale copy here would test the wrong shape. If it has not landed, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ['task-48932becda314704aad652b49a8d2209'] and stop. (b) VERIFY CONSTRAINT (1) YOURSELF, because the whole row is worthless if it is wrong: `grep -n 'codex' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts` gives the selector `/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu`. Confirm by eye that `agent-codex.cmd` does NOT match it (the character before "codex" is a hyphen, which is neither a path separator nor start-of-string) while `codex.cmd` does. writeAgentShim at tests/e2e/foundation/j1-loop-harness.ts:320-343 emits `agent-${arm}.cmd` / `agent-${arm}.sh` - so the existing writer CANNOT produce a codex-selecting shim, and this row needs its own. (c) SETTLE THE V2 QUESTION THE DESCRIPTION LEAVES OPEN (its constraint 3). daemon-v2-command-registry.ts:211 withholds `planning.submit_decomposition` from the v2 registry. MEASURED: `grep -rn 'cutover' tests/e2e/foundation/*.ts` finds only three comment mentions and NO dispatch, and the v2 plane is reached only through `provideV2` after the cutover marker - so an e2e daemon on a fresh store serves the V1 registry and the withheld set does not apply. VERIFY that on your own harness before writing the arm: if your journey's daemon does run the marker, assert the exact roster refusal instead, and say which branch you took. Do not discover this at the assertion. (d) READ THE PEER WIP, DO NOT BUILD ON IT. `tests/e2e/foundation/j5-compiler-agent.mjs` (289 lines) and `j5-plan-reject-harness.ts` are BOTH UNTRACKED (`git status --porcelain` = `??`) - live peer work, almost certainly task-2c016c04's. j5-compiler-agent.mjs is the closest existing model for the PLANNING lane (it calls planning_submit_decomposition, work_get_context and work_release as real tools/call frames) and its header explains why it is separate from fake-agent.mjs. READ IT FOR SHAPE. Never edit it, never import it, and never make this row's journey depend on it landing - it may change or vanish. Your named model stays the TRACKED one: fake-agent.mjs. (e) NOTE A GATE HAZARD THIS CREATES: `pnpm test:e2e` runs `tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json` FIRST and that tsconfig's include is `["./*.ts"]`, so the untracked `j5-plan-reject-harness.ts` IS in the type program. A type error there fails the whole leg before one test runs, and it is FOREIGN. Record the baseline now: run `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` standalone and quote each count line - plus any tsc failure verbatim, so step 5 can subtract it.

THE CODEX DOUBLE. NEW FILE tests/e2e/foundation/codex-agent.mjs. PLAIN `.mjs`, node builtins only, no TypeScript, no dependency, and deliberately NOT added to tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json - its include is `["./*.ts"]`, so a `.mjs` stays out of the type program by construction, exactly as fake-agent.mjs and j5-compiler-agent.mjs do. Copy fake-agent.mjs's WIRE shape line for line: initialize the MCP session over HTTP, then real JSON-RPC `tools/call` frames; NEVER touch the store. THE ONE THING THAT INVERTS, and it is the reason this double cannot be an arm on fake-agent.mjs: a claude seat receives a JSON file at `--mcp-config` carrying both origin and bearer, while a CODEX seat receives NEITHER. Measured at agent-spawner.ts: the bearer arrives in the child's OWN environment under CODEX_BEARER_VARIABLE (`MOE_AGENT_MCP_BEARER`, injected at :156 AFTER the agentEnvironment spread, pinned by agent-spawner.test.ts:291), and the origin arrives as the argv pair `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.url=<origin>`. So this double reads its bearer from `process.env` and parses its origin off argv - the exact inverse of fake-agent.mjs, whose header states it treats argv flags as non-evidence. Write that inversion into this file's own header, naming both files, so the next reader does not try to unify them. WRITE THE HEADER FIRST and make it carry: why plain .mjs; why the credential path is inverted; and that the file must be named so the spawner's codex regex selects it (step 3). COVER BOTH LANES IN ONE DOUBLE, branching on the mission the way the wrapper does - the planning lane (planning_submit_decomposition) and the code lane (review_submit) - because what makes this double codex-specific is the credential inversion, which both lanes need; two codex doubles would duplicate that inversion twice. Include an `--arm` flag with a NEGATIVE arm that exits 0 WITHOUT submitting, mirroring fake-agent.mjs's `skip-review`: DoD-2 requires a double that exits clean but lands nothing to FAIL the journey, and that arm is the only way to prove the journey reads the store rather than the exit code.

THE SHIM WRITER, NAMED SO THE CODEX BRANCH IS ACTUALLY SELECTED. NEW FILE tests/e2e/foundation/codex-journey-harness.ts (a `.ts`, so it IS in the tsc program - keep it clean or the whole e2e leg fails at tsc). Write a shim whose BASENAME IS EXACTLY `codex.cmd` (Windows) or `codex.sh` (POSIX) - not `agent-codex.*`, not `codex-seat.*`. Put it in its OWN directory under the scratch root so the bare name cannot collide with another arm's shim, since every arm otherwise distinguishes itself by filename and this one cannot. Copy the two facts writeAgentShim's docblock records at j1-loop-harness.ts:312-318, because both still bind: `agentSpawnInvocation` quotes the COMMAND ITSELF for cmd.exe so a multi-word MOE_AGENT_COMMAND becomes one unusable token - the shim must name `node` and prepend this run's argv; and `agentEnvironment()` scrubs every non-allowlisted key and drops all `MOE_*`, so NO env var reaches the double except the bearer the spawner itself injects after that scrub. Anything else this double needs (an echo directory, the arm) travels on the shim's own argv. DO NOT extend writeAgentShim to take a provider: it is on the hot path of five tracked journeys, its `agent-${arm}` naming is load-bearing for them, and this row's rail forbids widening a shared double to serve two providers - the same reasoning applies to its shim writer. Reuse the harness pieces that are TRACKED and provider-agnostic: the daemon/wrapper process control and store environment in j1-loop-harness.ts, and the durable readback in j1-ledger-view.ts (247 lines) - importing them is fine, editing them is not.

THE JOURNEY. NEW FILE tests/e2e/foundation/codex-seat-loop.e2e.test.ts. Drive the real wrapper against a real daemon with the codex shim as MOE_AGENT_COMMAND, and assert EVERY verdict from the DURABLE STORE AFTER THE PROCESSES ARE DEAD - never from the double's exit code, never from its stdout (DoD-2). j1-ledger-view.ts is the readback model. FIVE ARMS: (1) THE HAPPY PATH, DoD-1 - the planning reads, then `planning.submit_decomposition` accepted, then a `node.deliver` reaching verifier ACCEPTED and lander COMMITTED. Read the sealed run, the verifier receipt and the landing sha off the ledger. (2) DoD-3, and read this one carefully because it is the arm most easily faked: the double claims, calls `work_get_context` for its OWN item, and RELEASES ON THE FIRST TRY. Assert the release decision is exactly `EFFECTS_COMMITTED`. "It returned" and "it did not throw" are both non-assertions here; the release path reuses the observed-version disclosure task-f99cec0b landed at apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-conflict-error.ts:53 (`conflictError(decision)`), so a first-try release means no conflict was reported, and that is what must be pinned. (3) DoD-4 - PROVE THE CODEX BRANCH RAN, and assert it on the SPAWN SURFACE, not on the shim's filename: the codex-shaped argv (`exec`, `--ignore-user-config`, `--skip-git-repo-check`, `--ephemeral`, `--sandbox`) or the bearer-in-env path. A filename assertion is circular - it proves only what the harness wrote. THE POINT OF THIS ARM: if someone later renames the shim to `agent-codex.cmd`, the regex stops matching, the CLAUDE branch runs, and every other arm here still passes while the journey silently tests nothing about codex. (4) THE NEGATIVE ARM, DoD-2 - run the double's no-submit arm and assert the journey FAILS: no sealed run, no verifier receipt, no landing sha, despite a clean exit. (5) The `planning.submit_decomposition` dispatch takes whichever branch step 1(c) settled - accepted on the v1 registry, or the exact roster refusal if your daemon runs the v2 marker. Name the branch you took in the test's own comment, not only in the step note, so a later reader is not left guessing which world this journey assumes.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS, recorded in the step note. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. ALL THREE FILES THIS ROW CREATES ARE NEW AND THEREFORE UNTRACKED (`??`), so global rail 13 fires in full and `git diff` is BLIND to every one of them - it is empty before, during and after a mutation. Back each up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) and prove restoration by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore; a PowerShell copy can silently no-op and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. Say explicitly that no tracked path was mutated. THREE DRILLS, restore and prove after each: (i) THE ROW'S CENTRAL DRILL - rename the shim from `codex.cmd` to `agent-codex.cmd` and re-run. Arm (3) MUST go red. If the journey still passes, the codex branch was never being selected and every other arm was testing the claude seat; that is the exact silent revert DoD-4 exists to prevent, so quote the red. (ii) Make the double submit but skip the release - arm (2) must red naming the missing `EFFECTS_COMMITTED`, not merely reporting a different count. (iii) Point the double's readback at its own exit code instead of the ledger - arm (4), the negative arm, must red. That is what proves the journey reads the store rather than the process. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains: `pnpm test:e2e` (the named verification command; quote its `Test Files N passed` line AND confirm the new test appears by name in the output - a journey that did not run is not evidence), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. REMEMBER `pnpm test:e2e` RUNS tsc FIRST: a tsc failure is not a test result and must not be reported as one. If tsc fails inside the untracked `j5-plan-reject-harness.ts`, that is FOREIGN peer WIP - disclose it verbatim with its exact failing lines, attribute it by the step-1 baseline, and DO NOT fix or delete a peer's file to make your leg green. Attribute every red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's three owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: does the double ever read the store directly (grep your own file for a sqlite or store import - the rail says the wire or nothing); does the bare `codex.cmd` name collide with another arm's shim in a shared scratch directory; does the double hang if the bearer env var is absent, and does it fail LOUDLY rather than silently skipping its submit; is the origin parsed from argv robust to the `-c key=value` pair arriving in a different position; did you add the `.mjs` to tsconfig by reflex; did you edit fake-agent.mjs, writeAgentShim, or either untracked j5 file. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the shim's exact basename and WHY (the spawner's regex, quoted); which branch step 1(c) settled for `planning.submit_decomposition` and the evidence for it; that the codex double inverts the credential path (bearer from env, origin from argv) and therefore could not be an arm on fake-agent.mjs; drill (i)'s red, verbatim, since it is the proof the journey tests codex at all; and that the spawn-surface parity is task-48932bec's and the live `codex exec` run is task-c090faae's, neither exercised here.

THE PLANNING-LANE PRECEDENT IS UNTRACKED PEER WIP, AND THE V2 QUESTION IS SETTLED. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 3 files, all new.

## The row's three measured constraints all check out

All three hold as written. Constraint (1) especially: `writeAgentShim` (j1-loop-harness.ts:320-343) emits `agent-${arm}.cmd`, and the selector is `/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu` — "codex" must follow start-of-string or a path separator, so `agent-codex.cmd` does **not** match. The untracked j5 harness writes `j5-compiler.cmd`, also a non-match. The existing writer structurally cannot produce a codex-selecting shim.

## What the description does not mention: two untracked peers in the target directory

```
?? tests/e2e/foundation/j5-compiler-agent.mjs      (289 lines)
?? tests/e2e/foundation/j5-plan-reject-harness.ts
```

Both **untracked** — live peer work, almost certainly task-2c016c04's. `j5-compiler-agent.mjs` is the closest existing model for the PLANNING lane (real `tools/call` frames for `planning_submit_decomposition`, `work_get_context`, `work_release`) and its header explains why doubles stay separate. The plan says **read it for shape, never edit it, never depend on it landing.** The named model stays the tracked one, fake-agent.mjs.

**This creates a gate hazard for this row's own verification command.** `pnpm test:e2e` is `tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json && vitest run tests/e2e`, and that tsconfig's include is `["./*.ts"]` — so the untracked `j5-plan-reject-harness.ts` is **inside the type program**. A peer's type error fails this row's named leg before a single test runs. Disclose and attribute; never fix or delete a peer's file to get green.

## Constraint (3) settled, so the worker does not discover it at the assertion

`daemon-v2-command-registry.ts:211` withholds `planning.submit_decomposition`, but the v2 plane is entered only through `provideV2` after the cutover marker, and `grep -rn 'cutover' tests/e2e/foundation/*.ts` finds **three comment mentions and no dispatch**. A fresh e2e store serves the v1 registry and the withheld set never bites. The plan states that as the expected branch, still requires the worker to verify it on their own harness, and requires the branch be named in the test's own comment — the row's instruction was "determine which before writing the arm".

## One design call the row left open: how many codex doubles

**One, covering both lanes.** The rails forbid folding codex into fake-agent.mjs, and j5's header explains why doubles stay separate — but the DoD needs both lanes, and what makes this double codex-specific is the **credential inversion** (bearer from env, origin from argv), which both lanes need identically. Two codex doubles would duplicate that inversion and give it two places to drift. The separation that matters here is *provider*, not lane.

Same reasoning for the shim: a **new** writer, not a provider parameter on `writeAgentShim` — that function is on the hot path of five tracked journeys and its `agent-${arm}` naming is load-bearing for them.

## The failure this row exists to prevent is silent

If the shim basename is not exactly `codex.cmd` / `codex.sh`, the regex misses, the **claude** branch runs, and every other arm still passes while the journey proves nothing about codex. That is why DoD-4 demands the assertion be on the spawn surface (codex argv or bearer-in-env) and never on the filename — a filename assertion is circular, proving only what the harness wrote. Drill (i) — rename to `agent-codex.cmd`, require that arm to red — is the row's most valuable artifact.

Two smaller things: a bare `codex.cmd` has **no arm suffix to disambiguate it**, unlike every other shim, so it needs its own scratch subdirectory or two arms overwrite one path. And **global rail 13 fires in full here** — all three files are new and untracked, so `git diff` is blind to them; every drill needs SHA256-vs-backup restore proof in a separate call.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
NO SPLIT: three new files, all under tests/e2e/foundation, nothing near a line cap, one coherent deliverable (a double, its shim writer, and the journey that drives them). Splitting would land a double nothing runs.

DECISION 1 - ONE CODEX DOUBLE COVERING BOTH LANES, not two. The row's rail forbids folding the codex behaviour into fake-agent.mjs, and j5-compiler-agent.mjs's own header gives the reason for keeping doubles separate (fake-agent implements CODE nodes, bails on any mission without `code node "..."`, and every path ends in review_submit; five journeys depend on it). But the DoD needs BOTH lanes - submit_decomposition AND a node.deliver reaching ACCEPTED/COMMITTED. What makes this double codex-specific is the CREDENTIAL INVERSION (bearer from env, origin from argv), which both lanes need identically; two codex doubles would duplicate that inversion and give two places for it to drift. So: one new double, branching on the mission the way the wrapper does. The separation that matters here is PROVIDER, not lane.
REJECTED - extending fake-agent.mjs with a codex arm: forbidden by rail 5, and its header states it treats argv flags as NON-EVIDENCE while the codex double must learn its origin FROM argv. Folding them makes both stop proving what they were written to prove.
REJECTED - building on tests/e2e/foundation/j5-compiler-agent.mjs: it is UNTRACKED peer WIP (measured `??`), almost certainly task-2c016c04's live work. Excellent to READ for the planning-lane wire shape; fatal to depend on. The plan says read, never edit, never depend.
DECISION 2 - A NEW SHIM WRITER, not a provider parameter on writeAgentShim. That function (j1-loop-harness.ts:320) is on the hot path of five tracked journeys and its `agent-${arm}` naming is load-bearing for them; widening it to emit a bare `codex.cmd` for one arm risks all five. Same reasoning the rail applies to the double itself.
DECISION 3 - THE V2 QUESTION, which the description explicitly left open. Measured: `grep -rn 'cutover' tests/e2e/foundation/*.ts` finds three COMMENT mentions and no dispatch, and the v2 plane is only reached through `provideV2` after the cutover marker - so a fresh e2e store serves the V1 registry and the withheld set never applies. The plan states that as the expected branch but makes the worker VERIFY it on their own harness and name the branch in the test's comment, because "determine which before writing the arm" is the row's own instruction and a wrong assumption here surfaces as a confusing roster refusal mid-journey.
REJECTED - asserting the shim's filename to prove the codex branch ran: circular, it proves only what the harness wrote. DoD-4 already demands the spawn surface, and drill (i) is what makes that assertion load-bearing.
